pages.title: At the bedside
pages.text: Give your tamed maid a day or night shift. Once she falls asleep, watch her speech bubbles. Make sure bubbles are enabled.$(br2)An all-day shift, sitting, lazing around or being carried won't trigger sleep talk.

pages.title: “Are you asleep?”
pages.text: Place two of your maids' beds within 8 blocks. Both maids must be asleep during their chatter hours.$(br2)Day-shift maids chat at world ticks 16000–18999. Night-shift maids chat at ticks 0–2999. Each tries to speak every 10–20 seconds.

pages.title: Listening in
pages.text: Sneak up to the beds. Once still, you can release sneak and look around. Walk within 5 blocks of any maid in the group and they'll notice you and fall quiet.$(br2)Stay more than 5 blocks from every member for 10 seconds to let them chat again.

pages.title: A little comfort
pages.text: Each bedtime chatter bubble lowers the speaker's Fear of her owner by 1, down to zero. Each maid can lose up to 5 Fear per shift per game day. Waking up and going back to bed uses the same allowance.$(br2)Important dialogue takes priority.

pages.title: What is she dreaming?
pages.text: Outside chatter hours, even a maid sleeping alone may talk in her sleep. She tries every 25–45 seconds, even with her owner nearby.$(br2)Subtract her Trust in her owner from her Fear of them to find the chance of a nightmare line.

pages.title: Nightmare odds
pages.text: Fear minus Trust · Chance$(br)Below 0 · 10%$(br)0–25 · 30%$(br)26–50 · 50%$(br)51–75 · 70%$(br)76 or more · 90%$(br2)Neither dreams nor nightmares change Trust or Fear.

pages.title: Waking up
pages.text: When your maid wakes during chatter hours, stand within 5 blocks and you might catch her saying, “Ah... I'm going to sleep right now!”$(br2)If she wakes from a dream, you can catch a sleepy remark within 8 blocks, even while sneaking.
